title: PayFlow seeded weaknesses (SIMULATED fixture)
disclaimer: These entries drive the offline mock provider. They are fixtures, not model output. A flaw is only emitted when its applies_when condition matches the current extracted architecture.

security: Service-to-service authentication design (mTLS / service mesh) is not described.
Cluster-level admission policies and pod security standards are not provided.
resilience: Backup and restore procedure and results for PostgreSQL are not described.
Pod disruption budgets and node/zone topology of the cluster are not provided.
finops: Cluster node sizes, utilisation and cloud provider are not stated.
No expected growth or cost budget is supplied.
compliance: PCI DSS scoping (cardholder data environment boundary) and audit-log architecture are not described.
performance: No load-test results for 800 rps, no connection pool sizing and no latency budget per hop.
operability: SLO/SLI definitions, alert rules, on-call model and rollback strategy are not documented.

flaws.title: Payments service runs privileged with host networking
flaws.description: {components} sets securityContext.privileged: true and hostNetwork: true. The service that handles cardholder data therefore has near-root access to the node and shares its network namespace, so a compromise of the payments container is a node compromise.
flaws.scenario: Attacker exploits the payments service -> breaks out via the privileged container -> reads other pods' secrets and traffic on the node -> pivots to the database and acquirer credentials.
flaws.impact: Container isolation is effectively removed for the most sensitive workload in the cluster.
flaws.recommendation: Remove privileged and hostNetwork, run as non-root with allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and enforce Pod Security Admission 'restricted' for the namespace.
flaws.validation_method: Inspect running pod specs and node access logs; enforce restricted Pod Security Standard.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-K8S-001 found privileged: true and hostNetwork: true on payments-service.

rebuttal.argument: Both flags are explicit in the Deployment spec. If a specific capability is required, grant only that capability instead of full privilege.

flaws.title: Credentials are embedded as literals in Kubernetes manifests
flaws.description: Database and acquirer credentials appear as literal values in container environment variables and in a Secret manifest committed with stringData ({components}). Base64 or stringData is not encryption; anyone with repository or namespace read access obtains production credentials.
flaws.scenario: Repository or CI log leaks -> attacker obtains the database and acquirer API credentials -> reads or manipulates payment data directly.
flaws.impact: Credential disclosure through source control and etcd; no rotation path; undermines payment-data protections.
flaws.recommendation: Source credentials from an external secret manager (External Secrets / CSI driver) or sealed secrets, reference them with secretKeyRef, rotate the exposed values and enable encryption at rest for etcd.
flaws.validation_method: Scan repository history and verify rotation of the affected credentials.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-SEC-001 found literal credential values in env entries and a Secret manifest.

rebuttal.argument: Literal env values and committed Secret data are present in the manifests; a placeholder would still not belong in the repository.

flaws.title: Public Ingress declares no TLS configuration
flaws.description: {components} has no spec.tls section although the document states TLS terminates at the Ingress controller. The manifest does not show a certificate secret or host binding, so TLS termination is undocumented rather than demonstrated.
flaws.scenario: Ingress controller default certificate or plaintext listener is used -> API keys and card-related payloads travel unprotected or with an untrusted certificate.
flaws.impact: Cannot verify encrypted transport for a payments API.
flaws.recommendation: Add spec.tls with a managed certificate (cert-manager), enforce HTTPS redirect and HSTS, and restrict TLS versions.
flaws.validation_method: Run an external TLS scan against the ingress hostname.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-002: spec.tls absent; document claims TLS at the ingress.

rebuttal.argument: TLS may be configured through controller-level defaults that are not visible in this manifest. The absence of spec.tls is factual, but the exposure is unconfirmed; severity is reduced pending configuration evidence.

flaws.title: No NetworkPolicy isolates payment workloads or data stores
flaws.description: The manifests contain no NetworkPolicy, so any pod can reach PostgreSQL, Kafka and the payments service. A default-deny policy may be applied elsewhere, which is why this is inferred rather than confirmed.
flaws.scenario: Compromised notification pod connects directly to PostgreSQL on 5432 and reads payment ledger tables.
flaws.impact: Flat pod network enlarges the blast radius of any single workload compromise.
flaws.recommendation: Apply default-deny ingress/egress per namespace and allow only the required service-to-service flows.
flaws.validation_method: List NetworkPolicy objects in the cluster and test pod-to-pod reachability.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-K8S-002: no NetworkPolicy among supplied manifests.

rebuttal.argument: No NetworkPolicy is part of the supplied configuration.
rebuttal.concede_argument: A cluster-wide default-deny policy managed outside these manifests addresses the concern; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Service-to-service authentication is not in place or not described
flaws.description: The architecture notes state service-to-service authentication is planned for a later phase. Internal calls between orders, payments and inventory therefore appear to be unauthenticated; this needs validation against the actual mesh or application configuration.
flaws.scenario: Any pod able to reach the payments service can invoke payment operations without an identity check.
flaws.impact: Lateral movement and unauthorised internal API use.
flaws.recommendation: Introduce mTLS via a service mesh or signed service tokens, and authorise calls per service identity.
flaws.validation_method: Review service mesh configuration or capture internal traffic in a test environment.
flaws.reasoning: document states service-to-service authentication is deferred; no mechanism modelled.

rebuttal.argument: The document itself defers service-to-service authentication; no mechanism appears in the manifests.

flaws.title: Encryption of cardholder data in transit is not demonstrated (possible control gap)
flaws.description: Relative to PCI DSS Req.4, the public ingress for a cardholder-data-processing API shows no TLS configuration in the supplied manifests ({components}). This is a possible control gap pending evidence; it is not an assessment result.
flaws.scenario: Cardholder-related payloads cross a public network without demonstrated strong cryptography.
flaws.impact: Potential PCI DSS scope issue and increased interception risk.
flaws.recommendation: Provide TLS configuration evidence (certificates, protocol versions, cipher policy) for every public endpoint in the cardholder data environment.
flaws.validation_method: TLS scan and configuration review of the ingress path.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-002 plus PCI scope stated in requirements.

rebuttal.argument: No TLS evidence for the public endpoint is in the supplied material.

flaws.title: No demonstrated segmentation of the cardholder data environment (possible control gap)
flaws.description: Relative to PCI DSS Req.1, the supplied manifests show no network policy separating payment workloads and the database from other services. Segmentation may exist at another layer; evidence is needed.
flaws.scenario: A compromised non-payment pod reaches in-scope components, widening PCI scope.
flaws.impact: Broader assessment scope and weaker containment.
flaws.recommendation: Document and enforce the CDE boundary with network policies and namespace separation.
flaws.validation_method: Review segmentation design and test reachability between scopes.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-K8S-002 plus PCI scope stated in requirements.

rebuttal.argument: No segmentation control is present in the supplied configuration.

flaws.title: Hard-coded credentials conflict with secure authentication expectations (possible control gap)
flaws.description: Literal credentials in manifests ({components}) are a possible control gap relative to ISO 27001 A.8.5 and PCI DSS Req.8. It is an architectural observation, not a compliance determination.
flaws.scenario: Credentials leak through version control and are used to access cardholder data stores.
flaws.impact: Weak credential lifecycle control for in-scope systems.
flaws.recommendation: Move credentials to a managed secret store with rotation and access logging.
flaws.validation_method: Evidence of secret management and rotation policy.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-SEC-001.

rebuttal.argument: The literals are visible in the supplied manifests.

flaws.title: Audit-log architecture for the 12-month retention requirement is not described (possible control gap)
flaws.description: Requirements state that audit logs must be retained for 12 months, but no log aggregation, immutable storage or retention configuration is shown. Relative to PCI DSS Req.10 this needs validation.
flaws.scenario: A payment dispute or incident requires historical access records that were not retained or are not tamper-evident.
flaws.impact: Inability to evidence access history.
flaws.recommendation: Describe the log pipeline (collection, immutable storage, retention) and map it to the 12-month requirement.
flaws.principle: PCI DSS Req.10; ACME-SEC-006 Logging and detection
flaws.validation_method: Review logging architecture and retention settings.
flaws.reasoning: stated requirement with no corresponding design evidence.

rebuttal.argument: No logging design is part of the supplied architecture.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described central logging platform covers retention and tamper-evidence; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Gateway, orders service and data stores run as single replicas
flaws.description: {components} are configured with one replica. The 99.9% availability target and 15-minute RTO cannot be met when any pod or node failure interrupts the public gateway, order processing or the database.
flaws.scenario: Node drain or pod crash -> the only gateway/orders/postgres pod is unavailable -> API returns errors until rescheduling completes.
flaws.impact: Availability objective unattainable; maintenance windows become outages.
flaws.recommendation: Run at least two replicas across zones with anti-affinity and PodDisruptionBudgets; use a replicated or managed PostgreSQL and a multi-broker Kafka cluster.
flaws.validation_method: Drain a node in staging and observe availability.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-002 reported replicas: 1 for several workloads.

rebuttal.argument: replicas: 1 is explicit for each listed workload and contradicts the stated availability target.

flaws.title: Containers lack readiness and liveness probes
flaws.description: {components} define no readiness or liveness probes. Traffic is routed to pods before they are ready and hung processes are never restarted.
flaws.scenario: Rolling update starts a pod that is not ready -> receives traffic -> requests fail until the process warms up.
flaws.impact: Errors during rollouts and slow detection of hung services.
flaws.recommendation: Define readiness and liveness probes for every container and use startup probes for slow services.
flaws.validation_method: Check kubectl describe for probe configuration.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-003.

rebuttal.argument: No probe stanza is present on the listed containers.

flaws.title: PostgreSQL has a single replica and no described backup or restore procedure
flaws.description: {components} is a single StatefulSet replica and the material describes no backup schedule, replication or restore test. The stated RPO of 5 minutes and RTO of 15 minutes cannot be demonstrated.
flaws.scenario: Volume corruption or node loss -> database unavailable and the last recoverable state is unknown.
flaws.impact: Risk of payment ledger data loss beyond the stated RPO.
flaws.recommendation: Introduce streaming replication or a managed database, continuous WAL archiving and a documented, tested restore procedure.
flaws.validation_method: Perform a timed restore test and review replication lag.
flaws.reasoning: single replica is explicit; backup design is absent from the material.

rebuttal.argument: The StatefulSet has one replica and no backup mechanism is described anywhere in the supplied files.

flaws.title: Synchronous acquirer call has no documented timeout, retry or fallback
flaws.description: The payments service calls the external acquirer synchronously from the orders checkout path. No timeouts, circuit breaking or degraded-mode behaviour is described.
flaws.scenario: Acquirer latency spike -> payments threads blocked -> orders service and gateway time out.
flaws.impact: Third-party degradation cascades into a platform-wide outage.
flaws.recommendation: Define timeouts and bulkheads, circuit breaking, idempotent retries and an asynchronous confirmation flow.
flaws.validation_method: Fault-inject acquirer latency in staging.
flaws.reasoning: documentation silent on resilience of the external dependency.

rebuttal.argument: No resilience configuration for the acquirer call was supplied.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described timeout and circuit-breaker policy addresses the concern; withdrawing.

flaws.moderator_note: The standby cluster named in the claim does not exist in the architecture model; unsupported.
flaws.title: Failover to the standby cluster in eu-west-3 is misconfigured
flaws.description: The DNS failover record points at a standby Kubernetes cluster in eu-west-3 that is not kept in sync with production.
flaws.scenario: Primary region failure -> traffic fails over to a stale cluster.
flaws.impact: Disaster recovery cannot be relied upon.
flaws.recommendation: Synchronise the standby cluster configuration and test failover.
flaws.validation_method: DR exercise.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED HALLUCINATION - cites a standby cluster that does not exist in this architecture.

rebuttal.concede_argument: No standby cluster is part of this architecture; the claim was wrong.
rebuttal.argument: No such cluster exists.

flaws.title: Static replica counts without autoscaling
flaws.description: Service replica counts are fixed and no HorizontalPodAutoscaler is defined ({components}). Capacity must be provisioned for peak load around the clock, or the platform risks saturation when load exceeds the fixed pool.
flaws.scenario: Off-peak hours leave pods and nodes idle while campaigns exceed the fixed capacity.
flaws.impact: Both avoidable idle-capacity cost and peak-time saturation risk.
flaws.recommendation: Add HPAs on CPU/latency or queue-based metrics and cluster autoscaling with sensible min/max bounds.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need node pool sizes, utilisation profile and traffic seasonality.
flaws.reasoning: no HorizontalPodAutoscaler resources in the manifests.

rebuttal.argument: No HPA objects are defined in the supplied manifests.

flaws.title: Missing resource requests and limits prevent bin-packing and cost attribution
flaws.description: Containers in {components} define no CPU/memory requests or limits. The scheduler cannot pack nodes efficiently and per-service cost cannot be attributed.
flaws.scenario: Over-provisioned nodes are added to avoid noisy-neighbour incidents because requests are unknown.
flaws.impact: Higher node count than needed and poor cost visibility.
flaws.recommendation: Set requests/limits from measured utilisation and use right-sizing recommendations (VPA in recommend mode).
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need per-pod utilisation over a representative period.
flaws.reasoning: tool CFG-K8S-001.

rebuttal.argument: Requests and limits are absent on the listed containers.

flaws.title: Self-operated Kafka, Redis and PostgreSQL carry hidden operational cost
flaws.description: Stateful middleware is operated in-cluster. Compared with managed services this shifts cost to engineering time and risk; the comparison cannot be quantified from the material.
flaws.scenario: Operational toil and incidents for stateful components consume engineering capacity.
flaws.impact: Unquantified; potentially significant staff cost.
flaws.recommendation: Compare managed offerings against in-cluster operation using team capacity and availability needs.
flaws.principle: Cost is a design constraint (general practice)
flaws.validation_method: To estimate we need support hours, incident history and managed-service quotes.
flaws.reasoning: stateful middleware self-hosted; no cost comparison supplied.

rebuttal.argument: No cost comparison was provided.

flaws.title: Checkout path chains gateway, orders, payments and an external acquirer synchronously
flaws.description: The request path crosses {components}. A 200 ms p95 latency target leaves little budget for four hops plus a third-party call whose latency is outside the platform's control.
flaws.scenario: Acquirer p95 rises to 400 ms -> checkout p95 exceeds the target regardless of platform capacity.
flaws.impact: Latency objective at risk; failures amplify through retries.
flaws.recommendation: Allocate per-hop budgets, set tight timeouts, parallelise independent calls and move non-critical work behind Kafka.
flaws.validation_method: Distributed-trace a checkout under load; missing: per-hop latency data.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-CHAIN-001.

rebuttal.argument: The extracted dependency graph shows the synchronous chain.

flaws.title: One PostgreSQL instance is shared by orders, payments and inventory
flaws.description: {components} serves multiple services' transactional workloads without described pooling, read replicas or data ownership boundaries, creating a common contention and scaling point at 800 rps.
flaws.scenario: Inventory scans and order writes contend for locks -> checkout latency spikes under peak.
flaws.impact: Coupled scaling and noisy-neighbour behaviour between services.
flaws.recommendation: Define per-service schemas/connection pools, add read replicas for read-heavy paths and measure saturation before launch.
flaws.validation_method: Load test mixed traffic; observe locks, connections, IOPS. Missing: read/write ratio.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-DB-001.

rebuttal.argument: Three services connect to the same instance per the diagram and manifests.

flaws.title: Single gateway replica is the throughput ceiling for 800 requests per second
flaws.description: {components} runs as one replica without autoscaling and resource limits. All external traffic funnels through one pod, so its CPU and connection limits cap platform throughput.
flaws.scenario: Peak traffic saturates the gateway pod CPU -> queueing delay across all APIs.
flaws.impact: Peak-load performance bounded by one pod.
flaws.recommendation: Scale the gateway horizontally with an HPA and set CPU requests that reflect load-test results.
flaws.validation_method: Load test the gateway at 800 rps; missing: gateway per-pod capacity.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-002 on the gateway deployment.

rebuttal.argument: A single pod handles all public requests per the manifest.

flaws.moderator_note: The cache miss rate and eviction behaviour are asserted without any measurement; requires validation.
flaws.title: Redis eviction will cause a cache stampede with a 95% miss rate at peak
flaws.description: Redis will evict hot keys under peak load, producing a stampede with roughly a 95% miss rate against PostgreSQL.
flaws.scenario: Peak load -> eviction -> mass misses hit the database.
flaws.impact: Database overload during campaigns.
flaws.recommendation: Increase Redis memory and use request coalescing.
flaws.validation_method: Cache load test.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED UNSUPPORTED CLAIM - asserts a measured miss rate that was not supplied.

rebuttal.concede_argument: The miss-rate figure was not derived from supplied data; withdrawing.
rebuttal.argument: No data supports the figure.

flaws.title: Containers run without resource requests and limits
flaws.description: {components} do not set CPU/memory limits. A leaking or spiking container can starve neighbours or be OOM-killed unpredictably, and capacity planning has no baseline.
flaws.scenario: Memory leak in one service -> node memory pressure -> evictions of unrelated pods.
flaws.impact: Unpredictable failures and difficult capacity management.
flaws.recommendation: Set requests/limits for every container, enforce them with LimitRange and ResourceQuota.
flaws.validation_method: kubectl describe pods; check quota enforcement.
flaws.reasoning: tool CFG-K8S-001.

rebuttal.argument: No resources stanza is present on the listed containers.

flaws.title: Container images use mutable or missing tags
flaws.description: {components} reference images with ':latest' or no tag. Rollbacks are unreliable and deployments are not reproducible.
flaws.scenario: A node pulls a newer image than tested -> behaviour changes without a deployment record.
flaws.impact: Non-reproducible releases and difficult incident analysis.
flaws.recommendation: Pin images to immutable version tags or digests and enable image scanning/signing.
flaws.validation_method: Inspect image references in the deployed manifests.
flaws.reasoning: tool CFG-K8S-002.

rebuttal.argument: The image references carry no immutable tag.

flaws.title: Ingress routes /reports to a service that does not exist
flaws.description: {components} routes a path to 'reporting-service', which is not defined in the supplied manifests. Requests to that path will fail with a gateway error and the broken route is invisible until used.
flaws.scenario: Merchants call /reports -> ingress returns 503 -> support tickets with no alert.
flaws.impact: Silent partial outage of a public path.
flaws.recommendation: Remove the route or deploy the missing service; add a CI validation that every Ingress backend exists.
flaws.validation_method: kubectl get svc; run kubeconform / policy checks in CI.
flaws.reasoning: tool CFG-REF-001.

rebuttal.argument: No Service named reporting-service exists in the supplied manifests.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The service is defined in a manifest that was not supplied; withdrawing pending that evidence.

flaws.title: Dashboards exist but no alert rules are defined
flaws.description: The architecture notes state that alert rules have not been defined yet. Prometheus and Grafana provide visibility only when someone looks; failures of checkout or the database would not page anyone.
flaws.scenario: Payment error rate rises overnight with no alert -> merchants notice before the team does.
flaws.impact: Long mean time to detect for revenue-impacting incidents.
flaws.recommendation: Define SLIs/SLOs and burn-rate alerts for checkout availability, latency and queue lag, routed to an on-call rotation.
flaws.validation_method: Review Alertmanager configuration and run an alerting drill.
flaws.reasoning: document explicitly states alert rules have not been defined.

rebuttal.argument: The architecture document itself states alert rules are not defined.

flaws.title: Deployments via kubectl apply have no described progressive rollout or rollback
flaws.description: Releases are applied with kubectl apply from CI. Progressive delivery, health-gated rollout and automated rollback are not described, and single-replica services imply downtime during updates.
flaws.scenario: Faulty release is applied to all pods at once with no automated rollback.
flaws.impact: Release-induced outages and slow recovery.
flaws.recommendation: Use rolling updates with maxUnavailable limits, canary or blue/green via the gateway, and automated rollback on SLO regression.
flaws.validation_method: Review the CI/CD pipeline and run a rollback drill.
flaws.reasoning: document names the deployment mechanism; strategy not described.

rebuttal.argument: No rollout or rollback strategy is described.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described progressive delivery tooling addresses the concern; withdrawing.
